From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>

Cc: 
Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Demo follow-up: proposed pilot blueprint and kickoff checklist (Hearthside)

Hi Olivia and Ethan,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great discussion and helpful context about your storefront personalization use case. Below is a concise recap + a proposed pilot blueprint so we can lock on success criteria and a realistic timeline.

Recap (call highlights):
- Goal: validate Redwood inference for product-recommendation ranking and small-scale personalization across 3 storefronts.
- Constraints: must run behind your VPC for PII controls; SLA target ~200-300ms p95 for blocking recommendation calls; team wants clear unit economics for 1M, 5M token windows.
- Integration: ingest of product catalog via S3 feed; live inference through API with SDK client or dedicated-pool connector.

Proposed pilot blueprint (6 weeks):
1) Week 0 — Kickoff (1 week)
   - Confirm success criteria, sample traffic, and security/barrier items.
   - Deliverable: pilot runbook + access list.
   - Owner: Hearthside (data & SSO), Redwood (pilot runbook).
2) Week 1–2 — Technical onboarding & smoke tests
   - Provision test workspace (Redwood Private/Dedicated preview), ingest catalog sample, baseline latency measurements.
   - Deliverable: smoke test report, perf baseline.
   - Owner: Ben Carter (technical onboarding).
3) Week 3–4 — Feature exercise & side-by-side eval
   - Run representative queries, measure p95/p99 latency, throughput, failure rates, and quality metrics (hit rate, business KPIs).
   - Deliverable: metric dashboard + sample event traces.
4) Week 5–6 — Compact load & go/no-go decision
   - Run scaled traffic for 48 hours, cost estimate for steady state, document rollout checklist.
   - Deliverable: pilot conclusion slide + recommendation.

Success metrics (proposed — please edit):
- Latency: p95 <= 300ms for 95% of recommendation queries during typical peak traffic.
- Quality: lift of personalization CTR >= 6% on test cohort vs. baseline.
- Reliability: error rate < 0.5% and no production-impacting outages for the 48-hour scaled run.
- Cost: 20% or better unit cost vs. current CPU-backed baseline (measured across 1M token windows).

Security/compliance items we noted:
- SOC 2 attestation required for Dedicated/Private (we can provide Redwood attestation + customer-specific evidence).
- Data residency: option to host in your VPC region (us-west-2) for pilot.

Attachments: pilot blueprint + blank success metrics sheet attached.

Next steps (can you confirm?):
- Confirm or edit the success metrics above.
- Share sample catalog extract & a production-like query sample (anonymized) by Mon 3/22.
- Confirm preferred kickoff slot this week or early next week (we have Tue/Thu morning PST open).

Thanks — I’ll draft the pilot runbook and loop in Ben and Marissa for technical & commercial items.

Best,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
